He was traded in the middle of his rookie season to the [[Houston Rockets]], and was again involved in a midseason trade to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2011–12. In 2015, he signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]], but departed after just one season, signing with the Timberwolves in 2016. ==Early life and college== [[File:Kevin Love defending Jordan Hill.jpg|thumb|left|[[Kevin Love]] of [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] defends Hill, then with [[Arizona Wildcats basketball|Arizona]].]] Jordan Hill was born in [[Newberry, South Carolina]].{{cite web|title=Jordan Hill bio|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jordan_hill/bio.html|publisher=NBA|access-date=October 23, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101202214556/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jordan_hill/bio.html|archive-date=December 2, 2010|url-status=dead}} After Hill's mother died of [[breast cancer]] when Hill was three, Hill was raised by his father and grandmother and later older brother and older sister.{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Sekou |author-link=Sekou Smith |date=June 14, 2009 |title=Jordan Hill overcomes tough road to reach NBA |newspaper=Atlanta Journal-Constitution |url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/content/sports/hawks/stories/2009/06/14/jordan_hill_nba.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090617071506/http://www.ajc.com/sports/content/sports/hawks/stories/2009/06/14/jordan_hill_nba.html |archive-date=June 17, 2009}}{{cite news|last=Baldwin|first=Mike|title=Jordan Hill: The NBA Draft's bounce-back player|url=http://newsok.com/jordan-hill-the-nba-drafts-bounce-back-player/article/3378509|newspaper=The Oklahoman|date=June 17, 2009}} His cousin, [[Trevor Booker]], introduced him to basketball. Booker, who is four months younger than Hill, also became a player in the [[NBA]].{{cite news|last=Lee|first=Michael|title=Trevor Booker hoping to play against cousin Jordan Hill of Houston|date=November 10, 2010|newspaper=The Washington Post|url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/wizardsinsider/2010/11/trevor-booker-hoping-to-play-a.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151022185105/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/wizardsinsider/2010/11/trevor-booker-hoping-to-play-a.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 22, 2015|access-date=January 12, 2013}} Hill attended [[North Springs High School]] in [[Atlanta]], and the parents of a classmate became Hill's legal guardians. After graduating from North Springs in 2005, Hill spent a year at a [[University-preparatory school|prep school]] in [[Patterson, North Carolina]], [[The Patterson School]]. As a junior in high school, Hill was ineligible to play on the school basketball team, so he showcased his skills to potential college coaches through an [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] club based in [[Smyrna, Georgia]]. At the [[University of Arizona]], Hill played three years with the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Wildcats basketball]] team. He left Arizona ranked fifth all-time in field goal percentage (57.8%). As a junior (2008–2009), Hill started all 34 games and averaged 18.3 points and 11.0 rebounds. He earned Honorable Mention [[2009 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-America]] from the [[Associated Press]], Third-Team All-America honors from ''[[The Sporting News]]'', and first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] and All-Defensive Team honors both from the [[Pac-10]] conference that year. ==Professional career== ===NBA draft=== When Hill entered the [[2009 NBA draft]], many had him high up on the draft board, possibly a top 5 pick in the draft. As draft night went on and [[Stephen Curry]] was taken by [[Golden State Warriors|Golden State]], it left New York to pick Jordan Hill. ===New York Knicks (2009–2010)=== Hill was drafted as the 8th overall pick in the 2009 NBA draft by the [[New York Knicks]]. Hill earned about $4.3 million over the next two seasons.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4320844 |title=Knicks lock in first-round pick Hill |author=[[Associated Press]] |website=NBA.com |date=July 12, 2009 |accessdate=April 25, 2023 }} Hill played five games in the 2009 [[NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 14.4 ppg, 8.2 rebounds, 0.6 assists, 0.8 steals and 1.0 block. His highest-scoring game was a 21-point performance against the [[Washington Wizards]]. Hill scored his first regular season points for the Knicks against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on November 6, 2009. Hill was traded 25 games into his rookie season.{{Cite web|last=Khan|first=Yaseen|title=NBA Trade Rumors: Knicks and Rockets Trade Jordan Hill for T-Mac, but Why?|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/346278-jordan-hill-for-t-mac-why|access-date=2021-07-28|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}} ===Houston Rockets (2010–2012)=== On the trading deadline on February 18, 2010, Hill was traded along with [[Jared Jeffries]] to the [[Houston Rockets]] as part of a three-team deal that included [[Sacramento Kings|Sacramento]] that saw the Rockets' [[Tracy McGrady]] go to the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web |last=Stein |first=Marc |last2=Sheridan |first2=Chris |date=February 19, 2010 |title=Tracy McGrady traded to New York Knicks in 3-team deal, sources say |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4924836 |accessdate=April 25, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2012–2015)=== At the trade deadline again on March 15, 2012, Hill was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for point guard [[Derek Fisher]] and a protected first-round draft pick from [[Dallas Mavericks|Dallas]].{{cite web|author=Staff Report|title=Lakers trade Derek Fisher to Rockets for Jordan Hill|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2012-03-15/nba-trade-rumors-lakers-derek-fisher-houston-rockets-jordan-hill|work=SportingNews.com|access-date=March 15, 2012|archive-date=March 16, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120316184247/http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2012-03-15/nba-trade-rumors-lakers-derek-fisher-houston-rockets-jordan-hill|url-status=dead}}{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2012-trade-deadline-tracker/ |title=2012 Trade Deadline Tracker | NBA.com |website=[[NBA]].com |access-date=March 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317215247/http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2012-trade-deadline-tracker/ |archive-date=March 17, 2012 |url-status=dead }} Hill played in seven regular season games with the Lakers, averaging 4.7 points and 4.4 rebounds in 11.7 minutes. In 12 playoff games, he averaged 4.8 points and 6.3 rebounds in 18.1 minutes. On July 25, 2012, Hill re-signed with the Lakers on a two-year, $8 million contract.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-re-sign-jordan-hill |title=Lakers Re-Sign Jordan Hill |work=[[NBA]].com |date=July 25, 2012 |access-date=July 26, 2012}} The Lakers struggled during the [[2012–13 Los Angeles Lakers season|2012–13 season]], but he brought hustle that was lacking in the team.{{cite news |last=Bresnahan |first=Mike |title=Losses keep piling up for Lakers |date=January 11, 2013 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/basketball/nba/lakers/la-sp-lakers-thunder-20130112,0,4684147,full.story |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130119012209/http://www.latimes.com/sports/basketball/nba/lakers/la-sp-lakers-thunder-20130112,0,4684147,full.story |archive-date=January 19, 2013 |url-status=dead }} On January 6, 2013, against the [[Denver Nuggets]], Hill suffered a major injury when Denver's [[Andre Miller]] drove baseline on Lakers teammate [[Kobe Bryant]], who inadvertently stepped on Hill's foot; however, Hill was also moving and pulled his hip. Surgery was required after doctors found loose fragments and a possible [[Acetabular labrum|labral]] tear.{{cite news |last=Pincus |first=Eric |title=Jordan Hill shocked and devastated by hip injury |date=January 12, 2013 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-jordan-hill-shocked-devastated-hip-injury-20130112,0,171937.story?track=rss |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116051313/http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-jordan-hill-shocked-devastated-hip-injury-20130112,0,171937.story?track=rss |archive-date=January 16, 2013 |url-status=live }} In 29 games, he was averaging 6.7 points and 5.7 rebounds in 15.8 minutes per game. His rebounds-per-minute average was among the league's best, prompting Bryant to lament Hill's absence after the Lakers were outrebounded during a game.{{cite news |last=Pincus |first=Eric |title=Jordan Hill has return time frame, but will the Lakers be playing? |date=April 11, 2013 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times 12, 2013, in the ninth game of the [[2013–14 Los Angeles Lakers season|2013–14 season]], Hill was a starter for the first time during the season and scored a career-high 21 points against the [[New |url-status=live }} ===Indiana Pacers (2015–2016)=== On July 14, 2015, Hill signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |date=July 14, 2015 |title=Pacers Sign Free Agent Jordan Hill |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-sign-free-agent-jordan-hill |access-date=April 25, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} He made his debut for the Pacers in the team's season opener against the [[Toronto Raptors]] on October 28, recording 8 points and 8 rebounds off the bench in a 106–99 loss.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/INDTOR/gameinfo.html|title=DeRozan scores 25, Lowry has 23, On July 20, 2016, Hill signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web |date=July 20, 2016 |title=Timberwolves Sign Forward/center Jordan Hill |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-forward/center-jordan-hill |access-date=April 25, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} On June 26, 2017, he was waived by the Timberwolves.{{cite news|title=TIMBERWOLVES WAIVE FORWARD/CENTER JORDAN HILL|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-waive-forward/center-jordan-hill|access-date=April 25, 2023|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2017}}
